reader.summary: Singapore's dominant story this week was the escalating haze crisis from Indonesia. The government expanded its crackdown, issuing notices to three more Indonesian firms and broadening its investigation to ten locally based companies, while a minister's blunt warning that firms cannot "play hide and seek" sent agricultural stocks lower. In a related energy move, Indonesia cut pipeline gas exports to Singapore by roughly nine percent. On the financial side, core inflation for September came in at two percent, slightly below forecast, while home prices continued to climb and rents surged at the fastest pace since 2023. Singapore also felt the cooling of Asia's 2026 IPO pipeline. The Singapore Exchange CEO signalled he plans to hand over the reins after a decade, with his contract set to end in 2027. GIC and Temasek were active in cross-border deals, including a joint venture with UK-based PHP to cut debt, and both denied instigating a rout in Indonesian equities. In technology, China's Moonshot AI posted a job listing indicating it will operate out of Singapore, and Horizon3 expanded its AI-native security business into the city-state. Max Verstappen took pole position ahead of the Singapore Grand Prix.

display.eli5:
Singapore is dealing with a really bad haze problem. Smoke from fires in Indonesia is drifting over and making the air unhealthy to breathe. The Singapore government is getting angry and is now going after more companies with legal action, not just warnings. Think of it like a teacher who stops just giving you a look and actually starts writing your name on the detention list.

At the same time, Indonesia is sending less natural gas through the pipeline that supplies Singapore. That is like your water company turning down the tap. Singapore will need to figure out where to get the rest of its gas from, and that is a practical problem the government has to solve this week.

The big stock exchange in Singapore, the one that lists companies, is about to get a new boss. The current CEO has been there for ten years and has said he is stepping down. The board will need to start the process of finding his replacement, and that is generating a lot of discussion in business circles.

A surprise would be if a major tech company announces it is building a huge new data centre in Singapore, which would be exciting for the AI industry but not what most people are focused on right now.

During the week of October 14 to 17, 2026, Singapore's most pressing issue was the Indonesian haze crisis, which pushed the city-state into its twelfth consecutive day of unhealthy air, the longest streak since 2015. Prime Minister Wong Lee Suen warned of further action, and Singapore formally placed seven Indonesian firms on notice over the fires, while weighing legal proceedings. Air purifiers and face masks sold out across the country, and pollution reached 'very unhealthy' levels. In a separate but significant development, a Singapore-registered container ship was struck by a projectile in the Strait of Hormuz and sank, though other vessels continued transiting the waterway. On the economic front, September exports surged 68.4 percent year on year, and the central bank held its monetary policy steady amid a 5.4 percent expansion driven largely by artificial intelligence activity. Singapore's minister declared the city-state is positioning itself as Southeast Asia's AI gateway,
